question: How does the yogin, by abiding without effort in the supreme lake of power, come to dissolve all constriction and attain the liberated state?
premises: Abiding without effort in the lake of power allows the yogin to discern only that supreme reality.
By dissolving constriction and traces of contraction, awareness becomes identified with that reality.
Through the graded practices cited, all outer supports are abandoned until only the state of absorption remains.
inference: When all supports are abandoned and awareness abides without appearance, the yogin turns away from the continuity of limited existence and abides in the supreme state of Shiva.
uncertainties: The precise referent of the fused token at the end remains unresolved without further context.
Several cited passages are abbreviated by 'iti-vat', so their full scope is only indicated here.
The technical distinction between the listed states of support is applied cumulatively rather than as discrete steps.
plain_english: Seated at ease, the yogin plunges into the supreme lake of power. Freed from all effort, inwardly turned, he discerns only that reality. Without needing place, time, or means, its upwelling appears in every form. By dissolving the constriction of body and its traces, he becomes one with it. Following the cited instructions, he abandons all outer and inner supports, fixes his gaze without fixation, and rests in the middle beyond both. With nothing conceived, mind placed in that alone, he becomes absorbed in bliss and equal awareness. In that state, all objects fall away; it is the liberated state of Shiva, beyond appearance, from which one turns back no more to limited existence.
